page: Microsoft Azure M4pds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration is built on a 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) and provides 4 dedicated vCPUs. Memory allocation is substantial, offering 64.0 GB of total RAM, which translates to a high density of 16.0 GB of memory per vCPU core. The server does not incorporate dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Storage provisions include 236 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity alongside support for Premium Storage tiers. This local solid-state storage delivers rapid temporary access for scratch files and volatile databases, though applications relying on persistence must target appropriate external storage services. Network configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring deliberate network design for external reachability.

Qualitatively, the 1:16 vCPU-to-memory ratio offers high resource efficiency for environments constrained by memory rather than processing throughput. The ARM processor profile offers an alternative execution environment where software ecosystems support ARM instructions. The instance architecture is suited for in-memory caching layers, relational and NoSQL databases, memory-centric ETL jobs, and data analytics pipelines.
